checks.label: Photo Picker Enforcement (Android 13+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else pm list packages 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'com\.google\.android\.providers\.media\.module|com\.android\.providers\.media' | head -1; fi
checks.description: Android 13 (API 33) introduced the system Photo Picker so apps can pick images/video without the full READ_MEDIA_IMAGES permission. The picker is delivered by the MediaProvider module; its presence is required for apps to use the privacy-preserving picker API. On A13+ this check confirms the provider exists. On pre-A13 builds it reports PRE_A13_SDK_<n> as informational.
checks.remediation: On Android 13+, ensure com.google.android.providers.media.module (Mainline) or com.android.providers.media is present and updated via Play system updates. Encourage in-house apps to use ACTION_PICK_IMAGES instead of requesting READ_MEDIA_*.

checks.label: Granular Media Permissions Granted (READ_MEDIA_*)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | sed 's/package://' | while read pkg; do for P in android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES android.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO android.permission.READ_MEDIA_AUDIO; do if dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "granted=true" | grep -q "$P"; then echo "$pkg $P"; fi; done; done | head -20; fi
checks.description: On Android 13+ the legacy READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission was split into READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO and READ_MEDIA_AUDIO. Enumerates every third-party app that has been granted any of these granular media permissions. On a kiosk, POS or medical device the result should usually be empty - the audit lets the operator confirm only intentional apps see the user media library.
checks.remediation: Revoke READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/VIDEO/AUDIO from apps that do not need direct gallery access: 'pm revoke <pkg> android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES'. Encourage apps to use the system Photo Picker instead.

checks.label: POST_NOTIFICATIONS Runtime Permission Audit
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | sed 's/package://' | while read pkg; do if dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "granted=true" | grep -q 'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS'; then echo "$pkg"; fi; done | head -20; fi
checks.description: Android 13 turned POST_NOTIFICATIONS into a runtime permission. Lists every third-party app that currently holds it. Useful as an inventory check on locked-down deployments (kiosk, POS, medical) where the operator wants to confirm only approved apps can raise notifications, since notification listeners and the Identity Check flow both interact with this surface.
checks.remediation: Revoke POST_NOTIFICATIONS from apps that should not raise notifications: 'pm revoke <pkg> android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS'. Review remaining grants against the approved app list.

checks.label: Foreground Service Type Declared (Android 14+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 34 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A14_SDK_$SDK"; else dumpsys activity services 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'ServiceRecord|foregroundServiceType' | grep -B1 'foregroundServiceType=0\b' | grep ServiceRecord | head -10; fi
checks.description: Android 14 (API 34) requires every foreground service to declare a foregroundServiceType (camera, microphone, location, dataSync, mediaPlayback, etc). A running FGS with type 0 on an A14+ build indicates either a legacy app targeting an old SDK that has been allowed to skip the requirement, or a service that worked around the new declaration rule. Either case is worth investigating because untyped FGS bypass the per-type runtime-permission gating Android 14 enforces.
checks.remediation: Identify the offending app (ServiceRecord shows package/class) and update it to target SDK 34+ and declare the correct foregroundServiceType in its manifest. Remove apps that cannot be updated and rely on untyped foreground services.

checks.label: Theft Detection Lock Enabled (Android 15)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 35 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A15_SDK_$SDK"; else V=$(settings get secure theft_detection_lock_enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && echo UNSET || echo "$V"; fi
checks.description: Android 15 ships Theft Detection Lock: the device uses on-device ML on accelerometer and connectivity signals to detect a snatch (sudden motion plus immediate disconnect from known networks) and auto-locks. On consumer phones used by field staff this is a meaningful loss-of-control mitigation. UNSET means the user has not opted in; 0 means it was actively disabled. Skipped automatically on pre-A15.
checks.remediation: Enable in Settings > Security and privacy > Device unlock > Theft protection > Theft Detection Lock, or push via DPC. For fleet deployments, enable this together with Offline Device Lock and Remote Lock.

checks.label: Identity Check Enabled (Android 15)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 35 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A15_SDK_$SDK"; else V=$(settings get secure identity_check_enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && echo UNSET || echo "$V"; fi
checks.description: Android 15 Identity Check requires biometric authentication for sensitive settings changes (lockscreen credential changes, factory reset, password manager access, disabling Find My Device) when the device is outside a trusted location. Defeats the 'thief watches you type the PIN, then locks you out' attack pattern. UNSET means user has not opted in.
checks.remediation: Enable in Settings > Security and privacy > Device unlock > Identity Check. Requires Class 3 (Strong) biometric. Combine with Theft Detection Lock for full A15 anti-theft posture.

checks.label: Restricted Networking Mode Active
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else dumpsys netpolicy 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'restrictBackground|restrictedMode|mRestricted' | head -5; fi
checks.description: Reports the current state of Android's restricted networking / data saver policy from netpolicy. Restricted networking mode caps background data for non-allowlisted apps and is a useful indicator on locked-down POS, kiosk and field devices where only the operator app should reach the network. Pre-A13 builds are skipped.
checks.remediation: Enable Data Saver / Restricted Networking in Settings > Network and internet > Data Saver and add only the operator app to the unrestricted allowlist. For DPC-managed devices, push the policy via DevicePolicyManager.setNetworkLoggingEnabled() and per-app background data rules.

checks.label: Advanced Protection Program (Android 15+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 35 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A15_SDK_$SDK"; else V=$(settings get global advanced_protection_mode 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && echo UNSET || echo "$V"; fi
checks.description: Android 15 ships an on-device Advanced Protection mode (the device-level counterpart to Google account Advanced Protection). When enabled it forces stricter defaults: MTE on supported chips, blocks 2G fallback, blocks USB data on lock, disables sideloading, hardens WebView SafeBrowsing. Recommended for journalists, executives, security staff and high-value POS/kiosk fleets. UNSET means user has not opted in.
checks.remediation: Enable in Settings > Security and privacy > Advanced Protection. Note this disables sideloading and some debugging features. For account-level Advanced Protection enrollment, see g.co/advancedprotection.
